NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (material substitution to corrosion-resistant alloy).  
Novel departure: Electrochemical potential shift via sacrificial anode array integrated into bolt geometry.  
Failure physics connection: Corrosion in splash zone is electrochemical; shifting local potential below iron's oxidation potential halts anodic dissolution.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Nernst equation for sacrificial anode potential (E = E° - (RT/nF)ln[Zn²⁺]). Magnitude verification: Zinc anode (E° = -0.76 V) shifts bolt potential to -1.0 V vs. Ag/AgCl, below iron's (-0.44 V), suppressing corrosion (CALCULATED from standard electrode potentials).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Components: Zinc alloy sacrificial anodes (shape-matched to bolt heads), electrically insulating shims (already-recorded: material spec from platform design docs), conductive coupling hardware (already-recorded: platform electrical system schematics).  
- Materials: ASTM B677 zinc alloy (stated material spec), fluoropolymer insulation (stated material spec).  
- Instruments: Potential difference monitor (already-recorded: platform cathodic protection system telemetry), pH sensor (already-recorded: splash zone environmental log), conductivity probe (already-recorded: seawater quality telemetry).  
- Procedure: Anode-bolt assembly replacement during routine maintenance (already-recorded: maintenance schedule log).  
- References: Threshold = -0.80 V vs. Ag/AgCl (DERIVED from stated iron corrosion potential and anode material spec); pH range 7.5-8.2 (DERIVED from stated seawater chemistry data); conductivity threshold >3.5 S/m (DERIVED from stated seawater salinity).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as bolt replacement (standard practice); no new structural modifications.  
- Operability: Passive operation; no power or controls (superior to impressed current systems).  
- Maintenance: Anode replacement interval (CALCULATED from anode mass and corrosion rate) aligns with standard bolt replacement cycle.  
- Cost class: Comparable to high-alloy bolts (standard practice); anode material cost offset by reduced inspection frequency.  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Monitor bolt potential, pH, and conductivity continuously for 30 days in splash zone.  
Instruments: Existing cathodic protection logger, pH sensor, conductivity probe (all already-recorded).  
Pass threshold: Potential ≤ -0.80 V for 100% of duration; pH and conductivity within derived ranges.  
Kill criterion: Potential > -0.70 V for >1 hour indicates anode depletion.  
Validation: Baseline established from existing platform corrosion data (stated historical records).  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Electrochemical potential (defines corrosion initiation per stated failure physics). Secondary indicators (pH, conductivity) supplement by confirming electrolyte conditions for electrochemical reaction.  

RISK  
Anode depletion rate may vary with seawater temperature (not modeled in existing data); requires periodic verification via potential monitoring.
